title: the Free Port Rising
premise: Dominic Ravensworth, a disgraced private security contractor hiding in the free port city of Vantara, receives calls on a burner phone from Mara, his former partner who supposedly died in the operation that broke him. She's alive, embedded in a smuggling syndicate planning to destroy a container terminal in an attack staged as an industrial accident, and she needs him because only he can read the port's security architecture. As Dominic races to expose the plot, he's torn between duty to his new found family at the harbor and the love he buried with Mara's memory. In the end, Dominic and Mara stop the attack together, but she chooses exile over surrender, leaving him to finally sleep through the night—grieving, belonging, and free.
about_author: Elodie Hartwell is a former maritime insurance investigator who spent a decade documenting accidents in ports from Rotterdam to Singapore before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people who guard things worth stealing, drawing on her obsession with the gray economies of free ports.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Dominic Ravensworth, insomniac and invisible, works dead-end contracts guarding warehouses in Vantara's free port. A burner phone left in his locker rings; the voice is Mara's—the partner he watched die two years ago. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: dread cracking open old grief.

chapters.title: Salt and Static
chapters.summary: The caller gives proof only Mara could know, then cuts off. Dominic digs out his old case files on the incident, reliving the explosion that killed his team. His landlord and only friend, dockworker Tomas, notices him unraveling. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into suspicion.

chapters.title: Free Port Rules
chapters.summary: Dominic maps Vantara's extraterritorial zones where cargo, money, and people vanish between jurisdictions. He realizes the burner phone routes through the port itself. Introduce Inspector Yuen, a customs officer who half-trusts him. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: the city revealed as a machine for forgetting.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Remembers
chapters.summary: Tomas brings Dominic into the dockworkers' tight-knit circle—a found family of night-shift cooks and retired riggers. Warmth he doesn't feel he deserves. Meanwhile someone searches his apartment. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: belonging offered, refused.

chapters.title: Second Voice on the Line
chapters.summary: Mara calls again: an attack on Terminal Four is scheduled within weeks, designed to look like a gas leak accident. She claims she infiltrated the syndicate but is now trapped. POV: Mara (first time). Emotional beat: her fear and her lie of omission—she helped plan it.

chapters.title: The Architecture of Accidents
chapters.summary: Dominic studies Terminal Four's blueprints from his contracting days and finds the exact choke point a 'leak' would exploit. Only three people had access to those plans. One is his old employer, Calloway. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: betrayal dawning.

chapters.title: Inspector Yuen's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Yuen POV chapter. She suspects Dominic of involvement when port records show his credentials ghost-accessing Terminal Four systems. Her duty versus her instinct that he's being framed. Emotional beat: institutional trust eroding.

chapters.title: Dead Drop at Pier Nine
chapters.summary: Dominic meets Mara's courier instead of Mara; the exchange goes wrong when syndicate enforcers arrive. He escapes through container canyons with a data drive. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: adrenaline masking terror—he's visible again.

chapters.title: The Drive
chapters.summary: The drive contains shipping manifests proving weapons-grade material moved through the port under diplomatic seals—and Mara's name on the original transport orders. Dominic confronts the possibility she's a perpetrator, not a prisoner. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: love against evidence.

chapters.title: Calloway's Offer
chapters.summary: Calloway summons Dominic, offers reinstatement and protection if he hands over everything and forgets Terminal Four. The meeting drips with menace. Dominic realizes Calloway may be the inside man—or another pawn. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: temptation of safety versus truth.

chapters.title: Mara's Confession
chapters.summary: Mara POV. Flashback to how she survived the incident, was coerced into the syndicate by leverage over Dominic's survival, and has been feeding them just enough to stay alive while sabotaging timelines. Emotional beat: guilt, and the cost of protecting him by lying.

chapters.title: Night Shift
chapters.summary: A quieter chapter: Dominic works a shift alongside Tomas's crew, fixing a crane under floodlights. He almost tells Tomas everything. The dockworkers' loyalty reminds him what he's fighting for beyond Mara. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: found family anchoring him.

chapters.title: Yuen Closes In
chapters.summary: Yuen corners Dominic with the ghost-access evidence. He gambles and shares the manifests. Uneasy alliance formed; she warns him the syndicate has friends inside customs. POV: Yuen. Emotional beat: two lonely professionals choosing each other's word over their institutions.

chapters.title: The Countdown Leaks
chapters.summary: Syndicate moves the attack up—ten days, not weeks. Mara's handler grows suspicious of her delays. She burns a safe house to buy time, deepening her cover at terrible moral cost. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: Trap at the Exchange
chapters.summary: Dominic arranges to meet Mara via the burner phone; it's a syndicate trap to identify the leak. He walks in knowingly, trades himself for her escape window. Captured. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: sacrifice as proof of love.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Dominic, held aboard a freighter, faces the syndicate's planner—who reveals Mara's full history with them and lets slip the true target isn't the terminal but the passenger ferry docking there during the 'accident.' POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: horror reframing everything.

chapters.title: The Long Swim
chapters.summary: Dominic escapes the freighter using port knowledge no outsider has, wounded, and reaches Yuen. Together they verify the ferry angle. Tomas mobilizes the dockworkers unofficially. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: broken man running on borrowed family.

chapters.title: Mara's Choice
chapters.summary: Mara POV. Ordered to arm the device herself, she instead disables its trigger remotely and transmits the real schematics to Dominic—exposing herself completely. Emotional beat: choosing him and the innocent passengers over survival.

chapters.title: Terminal Four
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Dominic and Yuen race to evacuate the ferry without triggering panic or alerting syndicate lookouts; Tomas's crew stalls the attackers' truck convoy with a staged crane 'accident' of their own. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: every ally paying forward small trusts.

chapters.title: Zero Hour
chapters.summary: Dominic reaches the device; Mara arrives on the other side of it, gun drawn by her handler. She turns the gun on him instead, kills the handler, and they disarm the bomb with ninety seconds left. The 'accident' becomes a foiled attack. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love and duty finally aligned.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Fallout: Calloway arrested via Yuen's evidence, the syndicate rolled up, Mara officially still dead. Authorities offer her witness protection abroad; staying means prison for her syndicate years. POV: Mara then Dominic. Emotional beat: the price of doing right.

chapters.title: First Light
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Dominic sleeps through the night for the first time since the incident. He shares coffee with Tomas's crew, takes a real job securing the rebuilt terminal, and posts a letter to a PO box in a city he'll never name. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: grief integrated, belonging accepted, love carried forward.
